titleText.es: ¿Sabes lo que ayuda mucho contra las crisis existenciales? Preguntarse cuánto espacio hay que dejar en la estantería para una colección de Terry Pratchett.
titleText.en: You know what really helps an existential crisis? Wondering how much shelf space to leave for a Terry Pratchett collection.
titleText.noteEn: The official English title text is preserved exactly; the Spanish archive gives a direct translation of the same shelf-space joke.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: collection; a gathered set of related things
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Colección is a feminine noun, so it uses una or la.

example.en: She started a coin collection.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In sin sentido, it describes something with no meaning or point.

example.en: The explanation makes sense.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hará is the future form of hacer for one person or thing.

example.es: El cambio hará que trabajemos mejor.
example.en: The change will make us work better.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; it links hacer to the caused action
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After hacer que, the later action uses its special caused-action form.

example.en: The music made them dance.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I lose; I may lose (special form used for a caused or uncertain action)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pierda is a special form of perder. The surrounding words identify who loses something.

example.es: No quiero que pierda las llaves.
example.en: I do not want her to lose the keys.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: at; begins en algún momento, “at some point”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here en introduces an indefinite point in time rather than a physical location.

example.en: We will discuss it at some point.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The complete expression en general means “in general” or “overall.”

example.en: In general, the plan works.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins en general, “in general”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The two words form a fixed expression about an overall view.

example.en: In general, I prefer walking.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: collections; gathered sets of related things
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is the plural of colección.

example.en: The museum keeps several collections.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you satisfy; you fulfill (one familiar person)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Satisfaces is the present form of satisfacer used with tú.

example.es: Con ese trabajo satisfaces tu curiosidad.
example.en: With that work, you satisfy your curiosity.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: It refers to strong sudden desires or tendencies.

example.en: He controlled his urges to buy things.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A urraca is a black-and-white bird popularly associated with collecting shiny objects.

example.es: Una urraca se posó en la rama.
example.en: A magpie landed on the branch.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In this contrast expression, aun is now commonly written without an accent, although the printed source uses aún.

example.en: It was late; even so, we continued.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Together, aun así introduces a result that remains true despite the previous point.

example.en: It was raining; even so, we went out.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here acabar describes the eventual result, not simply finishing an object.

example.en: If you do not ask, you end up waiting.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Muriendo is the irregular -iendo form of morir.

example.en: The plant is dying.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I confuse; I mistake one thing for another
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Use con before the second thing in confundo X con Y.

example.es: A veces confundo la sal con el azúcar.
example.en: Sometimes I mistake salt for sugar.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The written form crisis is the same in singular and plural; nearby words reveal the number.

example.en: The two crises ended quickly.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: It describes questions or crises about existence, meaning, or purpose.

example.en: They debated existential questions.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: with; introduces the second thing in a mix-up
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The pattern is confundir X con Y: to confuse or mistake X for Y.

example.es: Confundí su abrigo con el mío.
example.en: I mistook her coat for mine.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: It is the ability to notice and understand things clearly.

example.en: Her insight solved the problem.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The ending -a matches a feminine singular noun such as perspicacia.

example.en: We need technical help.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: marks the person or thing that cares, or for whom something matters
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The thing that matters controls the form of importar; le identifies the one who cares.

example.es: A Marta le importa el resultado.
example.en: Marta cares about the result.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I matter; I am important to someone
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Importo is the first-person singular form of importar in the sense of mattering.

example.es: Sé que importo a mis amigos.
example.en: I know that I matter to my friends.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is pointless or meaningless?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The same expression can describe an action, statement, plan, or situation that lacks meaning or a reasonable point.

example.en: The argument seemed pointless.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say “at some point” without specifying when?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Algún comes before the masculine noun momento; the expression can refer to the past or future according to the verb.

example.en: We will see each other at some point.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce an overall view rather than one specific case?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: It can appear at the beginning or end of a statement and means “in general” or “overall.”

example.es: La ciudad es tranquila en general.
example.en: The city is quiet overall.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say “even so” or “nevertheless”?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use aun así; the spelling aún así is also widespread.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The expression introduces something that remains true despite the preceding difficulty or contrast. Current standard spelling normally omits the accent when aun means “even.”

example.en: She was tired; even so, she finished.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone eventually ends up doing something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of acabar followed by the action form ending in -ando or -iendo.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The plus sign means “followed by.” Acabar changes for the person and time; the following action expresses the eventual result: acaba aceptando, acabaron riendo.

example.en: They always end up talking about work.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone mistakes one thing for another?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of confundir, name the first thing, add con, then name the second thing.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: X and Y are placeholders for the two complete items being mixed up. The verb changes for the person and time, but con remains unchanged.

example.es: Confundieron la entrada con la salida.
example.en: They mistook the entrance for the exit.

applications.explanationEn: Hará que introduces a future caused result, while pierda is the special form of perder used for that caused action; los is the visible object of pierda.
Los stands before the changed verb pierda and replaces the masculine plural things that may be lost.
En algún momento leaves the future time deliberately unspecified.

applications.explanationEn: Haciendo is the -iendo form that presents making collections as the means by which the following result occurs.
Aún así introduces a result that remains true despite the satisfaction just mentioned; this follows the source's accented spelling.
Acabas changes for one familiar listener, and muriendo names the eventual action using its -iendo form.

applications.explanationEn: A veces forms the fixed expression for something that happens sometimes.

applications.exampleEs: CONFUNDO TUS CRISIS EXISTENCIALES CON PERSPICACIA TÉCNICA
applications.explanationEn: Confundo names the mix-up, tus crisis existenciales fills the first complete item, con introduces the comparison, and perspicacia técnica fills the second complete item.
Crisis names the things first, and existenciales follows to describe their kind.
Existenciales uses its plural form to match the plural meaning of crisis.
Perspicacia names the quality first, and técnica follows to describe its domain.
Técnica uses feminine singular -a to match the feminine singular noun perspicacia.

applications.explanationEn: A veces forms the fixed expression for something that happens sometimes.
Confundo names the mix-up, esto fills the first item, con introduces the comparison, and un universo fills the second item.
Al combines a with el before relative que, referring back to the masculine singular noun universo.
Le identifies the universe as the entity that cares, while importo agrees with the first-person thing that matters.
